entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The 1957–1958 influenza pandemic was a global outbreak of the H2N2 virus, sweeping across the world and infecting millions. This pandemic, also known as the Asian flu, originated in East Asia and quickly spread to other parts of the globe, claiming over a million lives and causing widespread disruption to economies and societies.

The pandemic was a major public health crisis, with the World Health Organization (WHO) playing a key role in coordinating the international response. The virus spread rapidly due to the lack of immunity in the global population and the ease of global travel.

The 1957–1958 influenza pandemic had a significant impact on the development of public health policies and the coordination of global health responses. It also marked a significant shift in the way the WHO and other international organizations approached global health crises.

One of the most striking statistics of the pandemic was its rapid spread, with the virus reaching every continent and infecting over 20% of the world's population in just a few months.
